title: Orchestrated upgrade playbook and tooling for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) retrofit
creator: Avery Kim
description: Create a robust, operator-friendly upgrade playbook and supporting tooling for Redwood Private customers to perform orchestrated upgrades and schema/data migrations across VPC and on-prem deployments. Deliverables include an upgrade orchestration CLI (rwuptool), a migration controller for the Private operator, explicit LTS channel support, rollout gate primitives (canary cohorts, staged rollouts, automatic health gating), and documented offline/air-gapped procedures for customers with no outbound connectivity.
background: Customers running Redwood Private have heterogeneous environments (K8s distributions, private registries, strict egress controls) and need predictable upgrades with minimal downtime. Existing ad-hoc scripts cause surprises for DB migrations, operator upgrades, and third-party dependency changes. This initiative reduces failure blast radius, enables safe LTS patching, and standardizes rollback semantics for schema migrations.
tasks: Design rwuptool CLI that sequences operator upgrade, migration jobs, and post-checks
Implement migration-controller CRD to orchestrate ordered DB and KV store migrations with idempotency and resume support
Add LTS channel metadata to release artifacts and expose channel pinning in operator config
Integrate rollout gates: canary cohort selection, percent-based traffic shifting, and automatic health checks tied to Console traces/metrics
Define and validate offline upgrade flow: signed bundles, local registry import, and checksum verification
Author runbook/playbook for SRE and customer operators, including preflight checks, rollback play, and incident signals
Add audit events and KMS/HSM hooks for upgrade actions to satisfy compliance requirements
Create end-to-end CI verifying upgrade from previous LTS -> candidate -> LTS across supported K8s versions
Produce migration test harness with synthetic workloads and long-lived KV cache snapshots
Ship initial docs and a partner-facing beta program for three customers
acceptance_criteria: rwuptool can run a full orchestrated upgrade in a staging cluster, including operator replacement, sequence-controlled migrations, and a verified rollback
Migration-controller exposes clear status conditions (Pending -> Running -> Succeeded -> Failed) and can resume after control-plane restarts
LTS channel metadata is present on release objects and operator honors channel pin for automatic patching
Rollout gates successfully prevent progression on failing health checks (latency/5xx/error-rate regressions) during canary cohorts
Offline bundles are verified by checksum and signature; customer can perform upgrade without egress
Documentation reviewed and signed off by Support/PS and two pilot customers complete upgrades successfully
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with PM, Support, and Security. Agreed LTS channel model and required audit fields.
2026-03-04: Spike completed for migration-controller CRD shape and failure semantics. Chose a controller-driven Job queue with idempotent migration objects.
2026-03-06: rwuptool prototype scaffolding in repo; implements dry-run preflight validations (k8s version, node disk, registry reachability, KMS access).
2026-03-08: Health gating hooks defined. Initial metrics: p50 latency, p99 latency, error-rate, kv-cache hit ratio. Console events will be emitted for gate transitions.

2026-03-10: Began integration tests: staging run succeeded through operator upgrade and a no-op migration. Identified edge case: CRD defaulting changed between versions leading to pilot failure; workaround implemented in migration-controller to normalize defaults.
risks: Complex DB migrations with long-running transactions could increase tail latency and cause cascading rollout failure
Air-gapped customers might have incompatible third-party driver versions in their local registries
Operator upgrades that change CRD schemas may desynchronize existing custom resources if not carefully defaulted
Regression in KV cache format could cause invalidation and heavy warm-up cost post-upgrade
mitigations: Enforce non-blocking short migrations where possible and break large migrations into incremental steps
Provide signed, versioned offline bundles with clear dependency lists and a validation tool for local registries
Add preflight schema compatibility checks and automatic resource normalization helper in the controller
Introduce cache versioning and a migration path that keeps old entries readable until background compaction completes
customer_communication_plan: Pre-upgrade: send checklist and run rwuptool --dry-run report to customer 72h before scheduled patch
Upgrade window: provide live progress updates via Console and a Slack channel to Support and customer contacts
Post-upgrade: automated smoke tests and a 24h monitoring window with rollback option if critical signals exceed thresholds
qa_plan: Create CI jobs that test upgrade paths between last 3 LTS releases and current candidate
Run synthetic workload (ingest + inference + heavy KV churn) during staging upgrade
Simulate operator restarts and node eviction during migration-controller runs
Verify rollback restores previous DB schema state or provides safe fallback data access
